newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama youths, police clash outside U.S. Embassy.
newsitem.headline: Panama youths, police clash outside U.S. Embassy.

text.p: Youths protesting possible plans to set up a U.S.-assisted international anti-drug center in Panama clashed on Wednesday with riot police outside the United States Embassy in Panama City.
Witnesses said police opened fire with rubber bullets after more than 40 youths, most of them students, fought with riot police and threw bags full of paint against the walls of the embassy.
They also burned an effigy of U.S. President Bill Clinton outside the embassy.
"We will continue this type of protest until we unite people and get them to take to the streets to defend our sovereignty," student Saul Mendez told the local Telemetro television news program.
Telemetro quoted police as saying one student was slightly injured and 15 were arrested after the clashes.
Panama started formal talks with the United States in July over the possibility of creating a Multilateral Counternarcotics Center (MCC) at Howard Air Force Base.
The United States will turn over control of the Panama Canal to Panama and withdraw all troops and bases, including the Howard base, by Dec. 31, 1999, in accordance with bilateral canal treaties.
